sections.sectionText: Title: Imaging Mexico "Imaging Mexico” (CRN 49964) explores how since the post-independence period in the early 1800s through the present, visual cultures have participated in and commented on the formation of national identity in Mexico. We will study a variety of textual and visual mediums including the novel, painting, sculpture, architecture, prints, crafts, photography, and film in order to analyze how these various cultural forms have contributed to a variety of national projects. Students will hone the capacity to speak and write analytically about various forms of cultural production using each medium’s corresponding terminology in Spanish. Students will also acquire knowledge of major historical, artistic, and intellectual figures of the modern period in Mexico and a familiarity with critical approaches to cultural studies. Class meetings will take place on Tues. and Thurs. from 11:00 am - 12:20 pm. Language of instruction is Spanish. This course fulfills 300-level course requirements for the Spanish major or minor. Enrollment requires completion of SPAN 228 or permission by instructor. If the course is full, students can add their names to the waitlist at go.illinois.edu/SPAN_waitlist

info: 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours as topic varies. Prerequisite: SPAN 312 and SPAN 320 or consent of instructor.

sections.sectionText: Topic Title: Bodies In this course, we will explore how various sorts of embodiment shaped and reflected cultural values and norms of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries in Spain. We'll discuss works that revolve around the significance of phenotype, of sex, and of "blood," among other notions; that instruct Spaniards about how to control the vagaries of our bodies; and that, every now and then, remind readers that bodies might be a source of pleasure. We'll study big novels, poetry, and drama, but also newspapers of the period, manuals, and other bodies of work. Prerequisites: SPAN 312 and SPAN 320.

sections.sectionText: Topic Title: Contact varieties in French and Romance: A methodological approach. This course will focus on selected studies of the production and perception sociolinguistics variation in French and major Romance languages through the analysis of the methodologies and results published in these papers. We will learn matched-guise and implicit bias techniques to study phonetic variation and basic search methods and statistical techniques (from chi-square to regression methods and discriminant analysis) to study lexical variation in larger corpora. Knowledge of programing is not required but access to DMDX, R studio, and SPSS will be necessary. Taught in French and English, with readings in French, English, and other major Romance languages. Pre-requisite: some form of introduction to Linguistics and/or Sociolinguistics.
